title: CRISPR-Cas-mediated Multianalyte Synthetic Urine Biomarker Test for Portable Diagnostics
protocol: Collect and prepare tissue samples from healthy lung or lung tissue with tumor nodules.
Homogenize tissues in pre-chilled phosphate buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.4) at a ratio of 200 mg tissue/mL PBS using tissue dissociation tubes for automated dissociation into single-cell suspensions.
Centrifuge tissue homogenates at 6,000 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Retain the supernatant in a new tube.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 14,000 x g for 25 min at 4 °C.
Measure the protein concentration using bicinchoninic acid (BCA) protein assay kit.
Add PBS to the sample to prepare a 0.33 mg/mL solution.
Add 5 µL of 6 µM FRET-based peptide substrate probes to each well in a 384-well plate.
Perform the reaction in triplicate for each probe.
Centrifuge the well plate for 10 s at 180 x g to ensure the probes are at the bottom of the plate.
Add 25 µL of 0.33 mg/mL tissue sample or 40 µM recombinant protease to each well.
Centrifuge the well plate briefly at 180 x g to mix the probes and tissue lysates.
Immediately begin detecting probe cleavage by measuring fluorescence with a plate reader at 37 °C every 2 min for 1 h (λex: 485 nm; λem: 535 nm) to monitor the cleavage.
Incubate 20-mer phosphorothioated DNA reporters with 3'-DBCO group (1.1 eq.) with azide-terminated PAPs with C-terminus cysteine end in 100 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.0) at room temperature for >4 h.
Purify the product on a high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) system equipped with an appropriate column for biomolecules.
Set the HPLC gradient to start from 5% A buffer, keep isocratic for 20 min, and reach 80% B buffer at 65 min with a flow rate of 0.3 mL/min.
Collect the conjugate product with retention time at ~31 min.
Dissolve 2 mg of multivalent PEG (40 kDa, 8-arm) in 1 mL of 100 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.0).
Filter the dissolved multivalent PEG with a cutoff of 0.2 μm.
Add cysteine-terminated DNA-peptide conjugates to the filtered PEG solution and react at room temperature for >4 h or overnight at 4 °C.
Remove unconjugated materials using size exclusion chromatography with a commercially available dextran-agarose composite matrix column on FPLC.
Concentrate the synthesized nanosensors with centrifugal filter tubes (MWCO = 10 kDa) according to the manufacturer's recommended speed.
Quantify the concentration of DNA in the nanosensors using ssDNA assay kit at λex: 485 nm and λem: 535 nm.
Store the nanosensors at 4 °C.
Measure the hydrodynamic particle size of DNA-encoded nanosensors by dynamic light scattering (DLS).
Concentrate nanosensors to 0.5 mg/mL using centrifugal filter tubes (MWCO = 10 kDa).
Load concentrated samples onto a carbon film-coated copper grid mounted on a cryoholder.
Observe the morphology of nanosensors using cryogenic transmission electron microscopy at 200 kV with magnification ranging from 10,000 to 60,000.
Collect urine for baseline measurement before sensor injection.
Restrain the mouse and apply gentle pressure on the bladder to void any remaining urine onto a 96-well plate.
Pipette collected urine (~100-200 μL) from the 96-well plate into a 1.5 mL tube after replacing the mouse to its normal housing.
Inoculate 6 to 8-week-old BALB/c female mice with luciferase-expressing MC26-Fluc cell line (100k cells/mouse) via intravenous injection.
Monitor tumor progression weekly using an in vivo fluorescence imaging system.
Prepare an injection solution containing nanosensors at a concentration of 1 nmol by DNA barcode in sterile PBS.
Inject 200 μl sensor solution in PBS into each experimental mouse intravenously.
Collect urine samples from healthy control and tumor-bearing mice at 1 h after sensor injection.
Use fresh urine samples or defrost frozen samples on ice.
Centrifuge urine samples at 800 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Combine the reagents as shown in Supplementary Table 2, add Cas12a enzyme last and gently mix the reaction by pipetting up and down.
Incubate the reaction at 37 °C for 30 min.
Run the reporter reaction, as shown in Supplementary Table 3, in triplicate using the product of step 2.
Add the reaction from Step 2 last and quickly bring to the plate reader.
Detect LbaCas12a activation by measuring fluorescence with a plate reader at 37 °C every 2 min for 3 h (λex: 485 nm and λem: 535 nm) to monitor the cleavage kinetics of the DNA reporter.
Centrifuge urine samples at 800 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Incubate the reagents in Supplementary Table 2 at 37 °C for 30 min.
Run the reporter reaction using FAM-biotin labeled DNA reporter on a paper strip from Supplementary Table 4.
Combine the reagents and product of step 2 in a 96-well plate.
Cover with aluminum foil and incubate at 37 °C for 1 h.
Add 80 μL of PBS to a fresh well of a 96-well plate.
Add 20 μL of sample from step 3 to the well containing PBS.
Place one lateral flow paper strip in each well and wait until liquid reaches the top of the strip (<5 min).
Look for the appearance of control and/or sample band(s) on the paper strip.
Take a picture of the lateral flow strip.
Quantify band intensity using ImageJ.
